requirements.statement: The backend shall retrieve the customer's leagues, teams, rosters by week, and league scoring settings through a read-only Yahoo Fantasy OAuth connection.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall persist the customer's selected leagues, teams, starters or specific players, and favorite teams.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend. Positive: select, restart, selections retained. Negative: no selection silently dropped. VCASE-AFC-PR-002.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall report each supported installed viewing app as installed through platform-permitted detection.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: each installed supported app reported installed. Negative: absent app never reported installed. VCASE-AFC-PR-003.

requirements.statement: The backend shall mark each game's viewing access as verified only from supported provider integration or explicit customer confirmation.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: verified marking carries basis integration or confirmation. Negative: installed-app fact alone never yields verified. VCASE-AFC-PR-004.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall apply the customer's review and override to all detected profile information and retained local-market information.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: override of a detected app and of local market persists across restart and feed refresh. Negative: refresh never silently discards an override. VCASE-AFC-PR-005.

requirements.statement: When Yahoo approval is absent at T_yahoo (2026-10-16T19:00:00Z), the backend shall accept labeled manual lineup entry built from ESPN rosters as the active lineup source.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: at/after T_yahoo without approval, manual entry activates and is labeled manual. Negative: manual values never presented as Yahoo values. VCASE-AFC-PR-006.

requirements.statement: The backend shall hold exactly one active lineup source from the Yahoo read-only connection or labeled manual entry.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: source query returns exactly one active source. Negative: switchover never leaves zero or two active. VCASE-AFC-PR-007.

requirements.statement: The backend shall monitor live NFL game events only for profile-relevant games during customer-enabled viewing periods.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: game with a selected player or favorite team inside an enabled period is monitored. Negative: irrelevant game, or any game in quiet hours, is not monitored. VCASE-AFC-PR-008.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall record the customer's selected schedule and game-day mode as the monitoring enablement.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend. Positive: mode change alters the monitored game set per PR-008. Negative: no monitoring outside the recorded enablement. VCASE-AFC-PR-009.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall apply current-viewing-context detection only through supported mechanisms while the customer enables that detection.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: enabled detection uses a documented supported mechanism. Negative: disabled detection yields no viewing-context reads (decisions label profile-assumption per PR-011). VCASE-AFC-PR-010.

requirements.statement: The backend shall label each monitoring decision with its observed-playback or profile-assumption basis.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: every decision record carries exactly one basis label. Negative: no decision ships unlabeled. VCASE-AFC-PR-011.

requirements.statement: The backend shall ingest scores, field position, possession, involved player identifiers, timestamps, and scoring corrections from ESPN's unofficial public JSON.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: each listed field lands in the event cache. Negative: schema-invalid response handled per PR-064, never partially stored. VCASE-AFC-PR-012.

requirements.statement: When the ESPN endpoint is unavailable or its contract changes, the backend shall substitute labeled replay fixtures for live events on every affected value.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment with fixtures. Positive: outage run marks every affected value replay. Negative: no substituted value presented as live. VCASE-AFC-PR-013.

requirements.statement: The backend shall emit alerts for red-zone opportunities, player scores, and close games matching the customer's fantasy selections and alert-type settings.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: each of the three types fires for a matching selection. requirements.statement: While heads-up presentation is selected, the TV app shall present each alert as a heads-up notification with Watch and Dismiss actions during third-party viewing-app playback.

requirements.statement: The backend shall emit alerts only for customer-enabled alert types.

requirements.statement: The backend shall emit no more alerts than the customer's frequency setting permits.
requirements.verification: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: restrictive setting yields fewer alerts than permissive for an identical event stream. Negative: no alert beyond the setting on any run. VCASE-AFC-PR-017.

requirements.statement: The backend shall suppress alerts during the customer's quiet hours.
requirements.verification: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: triggering event inside quiet hours emits nothing. Negative: no quiet-hours alert on any run. VCASE-AFC-PR-018.

requirements.statement: The backend shall emit alerts only during the customer's game-day periods.
requirements.verification: Test, system, backend + settings UI. Positive: triggering event inside a game-day period emits (subject to other filters). Negative: nothing emits outside game-day periods. VCASE-AFC-PR-019.

requirements.statement: The backend shall delay each alert by the customer's spoiler delay.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: delivery timestamp minus event timestamp is at least the set delay. Negative: no alert delivered early. VCASE-AFC-PR-020.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall render each alert in the customer's chosen notification presentation.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: each offered presentation renders as chosen. Negative: panel-only choice shows no heads-up. VCASE-AFC-PR-021.

requirements.statement: The TV app shall announce alerts by voice only while the customer enables voice announcements over an implemented and verified voice route.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, tv-app, real stick (SD-001). Positive: enabled announcements speak over the verified route. Negative: no voice when disabled or when the route is unverified. VCASE-AFC-PR-022.

requirements.statement: The backend shall attach excitement commentary to an alert only at or below the customer's excitement level with every named entity grounded in the triggering event data.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: every named entity in commentary appears in the triggering event data. requirements.statement: The backend shall resolve player and event identifiers across providers to single identities.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: same player/event across sources resolves to one identity. Negative: no two identities for one entity, no merged distinct entities. VCASE-AFC-PR-024.

requirements.statement: The backend shall emit at most one alert per resolved event.
requirements.verification: Test, backend, AWS deployment. Positive: repeated retrieval of an unchanged event emits nothing further. Negative: no second alert for one resolved event. VCASE-AFC-PR-025.

requirements.statement: The backend shall propagate each scoring correction to previously emitted alerts and panel state.
requirements.verification: Test, system, AWS deployment. Positive: correction updates the alert record and the panel value. Negative: no corrected fact left stale in either surface. VCASE-AFC-PR-026.

requirements.statement: Each alert shall carry the verified player and matchup context that triggered it.
requirements.verification: Demonstration, system, real stick (SD-001) + backend. Positive: alert shows the triggering player and matchup from lineup and feed data. Negative: no alert without its triggering context. VCASE-AFC-PR-027.

requirements.statement: The system shall withhold any claim that a team red-zone entry proves a particular player is on the field or will score.
requirements.verification: Test, system, backend + TV surfaces. Positive: red-zone alert text makes only team-level claims. Negative: any player-on-field or will-score claim from a red-zone entry fails. VCASE-AFC-PR-028.

requirements.statement: The backend shall resolve each alerted event to an available provider and channel from the customer's installed apps, verified subscriptions, local market, and provider preference.

risks.control: If P2-X01 finds Fire OS 5, an API level below min_sdk, or a stick that cannot run the provider apps, then the program shall stop dependent device slices and raise a class C owner stop; it shall not buy a device or switch platform.
risks.recovery: Owner decides; device-independent backend and docs work continues.

risks.risk: Fire OS notification behavior over third-party playback is documented only for 2020.
risks.control: If P2-X02 shows no supported heads-up notification over provider playback, then the verdict shall name the exact limitation and the program shall raise a class C owner stop before AFC-PR-015 product code; it shall not substitute a phone screen or a companion-app-only alert silently.
risks.recovery: Owner decides scope; the rest continues.

risks.risk: Provider deep-link contracts may be private.
risks.control: If no supported provider game or channel link exists for a provider, then the resolver and launcher shall report the strongest observed outcome (`searchOpened`, `appHomeOpened`, `appAbsent`, `accessUnknown`, `playbackDenied`) honestly and the verdict shall record the missing interface as an integration gap; no outcome is relabeled `gameOpened`.
risks.recovery: Honest outcome; integration gap documented for the write-up.

risks.risk: Third-party video composition is not a documented public capability.
risks.control: If the panel spike fails or reaches spike_panel_max, then the panel shall be built as `PanelMode.fullScreen` (AFC-PR-047) with alerts and Watch still routed to the real provider apps (AFC-PR-048).

risks.risk: Unofficial JSON can change without notice.
risks.control: If the ESPN endpoint is unavailable or its contract changes, then ingest shall serve labeled replay fixtures for every affected value (AFC-PR-013) and reject schema-invalid responses without mutation (AFC-PR-064); the ESPN terms question shall be presented to the owner before submission (C3).

risks.risk: Yahoo review time is outside our control (Q7 not yet submitted).
risks.control: If Yahoo approval is absent at T_yahoo, then P2-X06 shall record a FAILS verdict for the Yahoo route selecting labeled manual entry, and the backend shall use labeled manual entry as the single active source (AFC-PR-006, -007).

risks.risk: The Free plan may refuse a service or quota.
risks.control: If any AWS action would require a Paid plan, a paid service or a payment method change, then the slice shall stop and raise a class F owner stop; no agent upgrades the account.

risks.risk: Only four live windows remain after approval.
risks.control: If a live window is missed or a game produces no qualifying event, then the slice shall use labeled replay of captured fixtures for repeatability and schedule the live check in the next live window; replay never stands in for live notification or provider behavior evidence.
risks.recovery: Replay for logic; live windows reserved for device evidence.

risks.risk: Provider apps commonly use secure surfaces that screen capture cannot read.
risks.control: If `adb` screencap or screenrecord returns black or blank frames for protected provider video, then the visual evidence shall combine the companion UI capture with window geometry from `dumpsys` and, if OD-AFC-P2-02 = A, an owner camera capture of the screen (OA-9); the demo plan shall mark any owner-filmed shots as owner-filmed and, if OD-AFC-P2-02 = B, shall use companion UI captures only for those shots.
risks.recovery: Geometry plus owner camera capture under A, companion UI only under B (OD-AFC-P2-02).

risks.control: If a selected route reaches a confirmed usage or rate limit, then the Orchestrator shall record the evidence and activate only the next approved fallback of the frozen profile with a class B receipt preserving coverage-assist and Reverify settings, or queue the slice; other errors shall not trigger a route switch.

risks.risk: S09 has merged; the Phase 2 product gate extension P2-G01 remains a prerequisite.
risks.control: If Phase 1 slice S09 (gate entrypoint) has not merged when a Phase 2 slice is ready to land, then the slice shall wait for S09 and P2-G01; it shall not land without a green gate run, and development continues on its branch with local test evidence.

risks.risk: Yahoo tokens, AWS profile names and provider account names can leak into captures and logs.
risks.control: When a secret, account detail, customer data or absolute local path is detected in material bound for the repository, release, video or submission, the program shall block that merge or publication until sanitized, and if exposure has occurred shall record the artifact without reproducing the value and notify the owner for rotation.
risks.recovery: Block and sanitize; rotation is the owner's action.

risks.risk: The deadline, device spikes and live windows constrain the schedule; the as-of remaining time is stated in Program plan.
risks.control: If a technical-wave release checkpoint W1..W5 is at risk of missing its due time by more than 12 h, then the Orchestrator shall present the owner a scope-reduction decision using the priority order in §Program plan, not cut scope silently.

risks.risk: M14 starts after A01..A05 (W3) with nine days to T_deadline and competes for the five-agent cap.
risks.control: If P2-V01 is not merged with its verdict table before the M12 submission documents are finalized (due 2026-10-22T16:00:00Z), then the submission shall describe the Vega build as in progress with its stated limits, and no M12 or M13 slice shall wait for it.
risks.recovery: Report in progress with limits; Fire OS path unaffected.

risks.risk: The host runs Ubuntu 26.04, newer than the documented test matrix.
risks.control: If the Vega SDK or Vega Virtual Device cannot install or run on the Ubuntu 26.04 x86_64 KVM host, then P2-V01 shall stop with the exact unmet requirement and raise an owner decision; no agent shall change the host OS, use sudo or install a system package.
